headline: Nifty looks set to open about 1% higher, near **26,000**, after Asia and US futures bounced. But 26,000 is the biggest wall of option sellers and oil jumped 4% overnight, so the rise may stall there.

mood.label: Positive
mood.why: Dashboard score +34 (leaning up), but only 2 of 4 checks agree; overnight news supports the open. Overnight data as of 08:47 IST.

key_points.text: GIFT Nifty (overnight Nifty futures) was near 26,070 at 7 am, about **1% above** yesterday's close of 25,819.
Brent crude rose **4.3%** since India closed, to $94.84, on a claimed Houthi attack on a Saudi refinery. Cheaper oil helped yesterday's rally, so this works against it.
The US proposed a tariff of up to **25%** on Indian goods (17% with a trade deal), likely not before January.
My call: the rally **continues at the open** but stalls near 26,000. A fall back below 25,819 would prove me wrong.
FIIs bought ₹4,479 crore yesterday, their **11th buying day in a row**, and Indian funds bought ₹4,019 crore too.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: Mostly good news for the open, supporting yesterday's rise; oil and tariffs are the clear negatives.

points.text: GIFT Nifty points to a gap-up of about **+250 points**. US markets are shut today for Thanksgiving, so Asia will set the tone.
US stocks closed slightly lower after hot US inflation data, but US futures are up this morning (S&P 500 **+0.6%**).
Asia is bouncing as tech recovers: Hong Kong **+2.2%**, Japan +1.5%, Taiwan +1.6%.
Indian shares listed in the US rose: Infosys **+4.2%**, Wipro +3.3%, HDFC Bank +2.9%. I couldn't confirm a specific reason for the IT jump.
Brent is up **4.3%** and gold 1.6% since India's close. The refinery damage is unconfirmed, so oil could ease, but for now it hurts India, a big oil importer.

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: Continuation at the open, slowing near 26,000; medium confidence for the open, low for the close.

points.text: For more upside: every overnight signal points up, and FIIs have bought **₹1.22 lakh crore** of shares so far in November.
Futures traders added bets on a rise: price up 1.85% with open contracts up **2.6%**.
Against: a 1% gap-up lands right at **26,000**, where the most call options are sold. Sellers usually defend that level.
Also against: oil's jump, the tariff threat and a likely US rate hike. Yesterday's 'cheaper oil' support is gone.
Proof I'm wrong: a slide below **25,819** means the gap-up failed; a close above 26,000 means the rally is stronger than I think.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The trend is up, but the checks underneath disagree.

points.text: Nifty is above its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages and keeps making higher tops and bottoms: the price check scores the **maximum +2**.
The option check scores **−1.29**: fresh calls were sold at 25,900–26,200, and many new puts look like worried protection buying, not a solid floor.
Put-call ratio (bets on a fall vs bets on a rise) is **1.02**, a normal level with no signal.
India VIX (expected swings) is 17.7, higher than **80%** of the last year's days and rising. Expect bigger moves both ways.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreign and Indian funds both bought yesterday, which is rare this month.

points.text: FIIs bought **₹4,479 crore** net, a big day by the dashboard's rule (₹3,000 crore or more).
Indian funds bought ₹4,019 crore after selling ₹60,528 crore earlier this month. **Both buying together** is a stronger sign.
In index futures FIIs are still mostly betting on a fall: only **23.8%** of their positions are bets on a rise, up from 20.1%.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: Markets are calmer this morning, but US rates and oil are real worries.

points.text: Dashboard red flag: 6-month US bills pay 4.44% vs the Fed's 3.88%, so markets expect a **US rate hike** in December.
The US 10-year bond rate fell about **0.20 points** this week to 4.86%, which usually helps foreign money flow to India.
The US fear gauge (VIX) is high at **28.3**, mostly on worries about AI-linked tech stocks.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: No Nifty 50 company reported, so results won't move the index today.

points.text: Siemens Energy India: revenue up 30%, profit up **81%** from last year. I couldn't confirm analysts' expectations.
Other filings were from small companies and don't affect Nifty.
No big-company results are due in the next week.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: OPEC+, India's GDP, the RBI and the Fed all land in the next two weeks.

points.text: OPEC+ (big oil producers) meets **Sunday, Nov 29**; it can cool or lift oil.
India's quarterly **GDP** is out Monday, Nov 30 at 4 pm; weekly expiry is Tuesday, Dec 1.
RBI rate decision on **Dec 4**; US Fed on the night of Dec 9–10. A US hike could slow FII buying.
Any news on the US tariff plan or India–US trade talks: a deal cuts the proposed rate to 17%.

levels.note: A close above 26,000 would mean buyers beat the biggest wall of call sellers and the rally has room; a close below 25,500 would break the floor and undo yesterday's rise.

watch.text: Does Nifty open near 26,000 and hold above 25,819 in the first hour?
Brent crude: back toward $90 helps, above $95 hurts.
IT stocks, after Infosys and Wipro rose 3–4% in the US.
FII and DII flow data. A 12th straight FII buying day would support the trend.

bottom_line: The trend is up, both foreign and Indian funds are buying, and overnight signals point to an open near 26,000. My read: the rise continues at the open but slows near 26,000, where option sellers are strongest. The dashboard leans up (+34) with low confidence, as only 2 of 4 checks agree. Main risks are oil and the US tariff proposal; a fall below 25,819 would show the gap-up failed.
